title: hybrid-leaky-reserve-orchestrator: continuous-batcher queueing + starvation mitigation
author: Evan Li
description:
Motivation: Continuous-batcher workloads with mixed short/long sequences still see occasional starvation and microbursts that push tail latency above SLOs in multi-tenant pools. This PR introduces the 'hybrid leaky reserve orchestrator' (HLRO), a scheduler extension that blends soft per-lane reserves, a leaky-decay reservation model, and a short-term spillover lane to reduce starvation and bound tail latency without destroying throughput.

What changed (overview): Implement HLRO inside continuous_batcher::orchestrator. Key ideas: 1) Soft per-queue reserves allocated from an elastic pool; unused reserve decays (leaky) so long-running heavy queues cannot permanently hoard capacity. 2) Spillover lane: requests that exceed a queue's current reserve may be forwarded to a short-lived high-priority spillover lane if probes indicate transient slack, reducing head-of-line blocking. 3) KV-pin-aware admission: requests that hold large kv-cache pins are deprioritized via a pin-weight multiplier to prevent starvation of lightweight requests. 4) Timeout jittering and staggered lease renewals to avoid synchronized preemption storms. 5) New starvation detector metric (scheduler.starvation_events) and per-queue telemetry for reserve utilization to allow ops to tune policies.

Performance: Microbenchmarks on mixed short/long synthetic traces show 12-18% reduction in 99th percentile token latency and 6% improvement in median throughput under moderate contention vs current master. Production canary on a ~200-GPU Dedicated pool demonstrated a 10% drop in alerting for queueing-related tail latency during weekday peaks.

Compatibility and flagging: HLRO is behind two runtime feature flags (continuous_batcher.hybrid_reserve_enabled and continuous_batcher.spillover_gate_ms) and a cluster-level knob for max_reserve_pct. Defaults are conservative and off for existing Dedicated clusters; enabled by default in the canary playbook we used.

Testing: Unit tests for reserve accounting and decay behavior, deterministic scheduler simulation harness additions, and end-to-end smoke tests in perf-canary. Added a small integration test to validate KV-pin weight math.

Migration and rollout: Recommended gradual rollout: enable on one canary zone for 24-48 hours, monitor scheduler.starvation_events and queue.reserve_utilization, then expand. Include fallback path to existing admission (config: continuous_batcher.fallback_on_repeated_spillover).

Files of note: scheduler/continuous_batcher/orchestrator.cc/h, scheduler/continuous_batcher/metrics.cc, runtime/kv_cache/pinning_policy.cc, tests/scheduler/hybrid_reserve_sim_test.cc, docs/design/hybrid-leaky-reserve.md, perf/canary/playbooks/hybrid-reserve-canary.md.

Risks and mitigations: Incorrect decay constants can cause oscillation; simulation harness was used to tune defaults. Spillover lane may slightly increase variance; gate ms and spillover rate limits are conservative by default. KV-pin weighting requires conservative multiplier to avoid throughput regression (default 1.2).

Related: ENG-12890 (scheduler SLO regressions), ENG-12902 (kv-cache eviction storms), SUP-8741 (customer report about long-tail pauses).

review_comments: Sofia Kumar: Can we reduce the global lock hold time in ReserveAccount? High contention could cause latency regressions in hot paths. Suggest using per-class atomics for common case. (requested changes)
Evan Li: Good point — refactored ReserveAccount fast path to use atomics; lock only on slow-path accounting. Added unit tests that stress concurrency.

Rohit Menon: The spillover lane looks promising. Need a clear abort path when spillover is repeatedly used to prevent oscillation. Add counters and an automatic fallback to normal admission after N consecutive spillovers. (requested changes)
Evan Li: Added spillover_failure_count per-queue and fallback config continuous_batcher.fallback_on_repeated_spillover (default true).
Aisha Patel: Observability looks solid. Please include the new metrics in the default dashboard and add an alert for starvation_events > 5/min. (approved)
Sofia Kumar: CI flaky test flapped once on first run; reran and green. Approving the changes. (approved)
ci_checks: perf-bench: pass (12-18% tail improvement on mixed trace)
release_notes: Introduce hybrid leaky reserve orchestrator to reduce continuous-batcher tail latency and prevent starvation.
Feature guarded by continuous_batcher.hybrid_reserve_enabled (off by default for existing clusters).
notes: Conservative defaults chosen; recommend staged rollout and close monitoring. If customers request older behavior, set continuous_batcher.hybrid_reserve_enabled=false and continuous_batcher.fallback_on_repeated_spillover=true.
